sourceNote: Selective DGT editorial notes for 2 Peter.

1:1: The Greek construction τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ most naturally identifies Jesus Christ as both “our God” and “Savior.” DGT preserves that grammatical reading.
1:19: “We have the prophetic word made more certain” can also be understood as “we have the very reliable prophetic word.” DGT keeps the comparative force of βεβαιότερον without deciding how Peter relates prophecy to the transfiguration experience.
1:20: ἐπίλυσις means interpretation, explanation, or unloosing. The verse says prophecy does not arise from one’s own interpretation; the following verse grounds prophecy’s origin in the Holy Spirit.
2:4: ταρταρόω is the verb “cast into Tartarus,” unique in the New Testament. DGT retains “Tartarus” rather than replacing it with the broader word “hell.”
2:18: SBLGNT reads ὀλίγως, “barely/scarcely,” in the phrase about those escaping people who live in error. Other witnesses have a different adverbial form; DGT follows the displayed SBLGNT text.
3:10: The end of the verse has an important textual problem. SBLGNT reads εὑρεθήσεται, “will be found,” rather than the familiar “will be burned up.” DGT follows its displayed Greek base text and leaves the striking wording intact.
3:16: Peter groups Paul’s letters with “the other Scriptures” (τὰς λοιπὰς γραφάς). DGT keeps the wording explicit rather than weakening “Scriptures” to a generic term.
